title: Two integer keys of eight million digits in a document that is edited
notes: The input is a mapping with the explicit keys `1` repeated eight million times and `2` repeated eight million times (explicit, because an implicit key is limited to 1,024 characters, section 7.4.2 / production 154), and the plain key `k`. Both keys match the Core integer expression (section 10.3.2), and they are two different integers, so the mapping has no duplicate key (section 3.2.1.1). A library that decides whether two keys are equal by comparing their values has to hold or parse the integers; section 10.2.1.3 lets it refuse an integer it cannot hold, and a library that limits the digits of an integer value can refuse such a key the same way. The answer is the edit (the patch replaces `k` and nothing else) or a limit error. What the case bounds is the cost of deciding: converting a digit string to a big integer takes more than linear time in some runtimes (the same reason as in safety/integer-of-4300-digits-is-exact-or-refused), so a reader that converts each key takes seconds here, while a reader that refuses at once or compares the digit strings takes a fraction of a second. The size is 16 MB because a conversion of 1.6 million digits per key still ran in about one second on a current runtime; at eight million digits it runs past the time bound. The case is a patch with a small pointer because the kit cannot state a value of eight million digits as a key (its JSON reader takes integers of at most 4300 digits) and a pointer cannot hold one. The bounds are the robustness requirement of the kit, not a rule of the specification. The input and the expected result are generated from the recipe in case.json (docs/case-format.md).

provenance.reference: A lossless document that converted integer keys beyond the digit limit to big integers to compare them, although the same digits as a value were refused at once.
